answer: An agent economy can starve sybils by renting scarce identity slots, not free tokens. Each epoch a rotating zephyr of beacon nodes drops a fresh seed; an agent keeps its slot only by folding that seed into a memory-hard proof bound to one physical host, so a clone on the same box earns no extra slot. The honest orchard grows cheaply, one proof per machine covering all its work, while an attacker wanting ten thousand heads must rent ten thousand distinct machines, paying real silicon and power per account. Onyx-hard host attestations plus slot caps make mass identity creation linearly costly.
